title: Software Construction practice bank
purpose: 60 practice questions for testing section quizzes

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a variable in a program?
options: Store a value that the program can use
Send every value to a printer
Delete the source code
Compile the operating system

questions.prompt: Which programming construct repeats a block of code?
options: A comment
A loop
A filename
A constant declaration

questions.prompt: What is a function?
options: A database backup
A version-control branch
A reusable block of code that performs a task
A hardware device

questions.prompt: What is a function parameter used for?
options: Removing all local variables
Stopping the compiler
Replacing every return statement
Receiving an input supplied by the caller

questions.prompt: What does a return statement normally do in a function?
options: Ends the function and optionally sends a value to its caller
Restarts the entire computer
Repeats the function indefinitely
Makes every local variable global

questions.prompt: In a zero-indexed array, what is the index of the first element?
options: The length of the array

questions.prompt: Which pair represents the possible values of a Boolean?
options: Red and blue
Integer and string
True and false
Read and write

questions.prompt: What is a typical job of a compiler?
options: Choose test answers
Store user passwords automatically
Replace the need for source code
Translate source code into another executable or intermediate form

questions.prompt: When does a runtime error occur?
options: While a program is executing
Only while editing a comment
Only before any program is started
Only when a Git branch is created

questions.prompt: What is debugging?
options: Writing release notes only
Finding and fixing defects in software
Deleting all tests
Converting every variable to text

questions.prompt: What is an exception in a program?
options: A required filename extension
A copy of the source repository
A signal of an unusual or error condition during execution
A guarantee that the program has no defects

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of version control?
options: Increasing the screen resolution
Replacing all software tests
Generating random passwords
Tracking changes to files and their history

questions.prompt: What does a Git commit record?
options: A snapshot of staged changes in repository history
Every file on the computer
Only the current network settings
An automatic deployment to all users

questions.prompt: What does a Git branch provide?
options: A second operating system
A separate line of development within a repository
A replacement for all commits
A guaranteed absence of merge conflicts

questions.prompt: What does a unit test usually focus on?
options: Every connected external service at once
The appearance of a physical computer
A small unit of behavior such as a function or class
Only the deployment budget

questions.prompt: What is the role of an assertion in a test?
options: Install the application
Hide failed test cases
Replace the tested function
Check that a condition or result matches an expectation

questions.prompt: What is a code review?
options: An examination of code changes by another developer
A mandatory rewrite of the whole application
A replacement for all automated tests
A way to remove repository history

questions.prompt: What is refactoring?
options: Adding a new feature regardless of existing behavior
Improving code structure while preserving observable behavior
Removing all error handling
Changing the programming language of every file

questions.prompt: What does a null reference usually represent?
options: The largest possible integer
An empty operating system
The absence of a referenced value or object
A successfully opened network connection

questions.prompt: What is encapsulation in object-oriented programming?
options: Making every field public
Copying every class into one file
Removing all methods from a class
Controlling access to internal state through a defined interface

questions.prompt: Which rule does a stack normally follow?
options: Last in, first out
First in, first out
Smallest value first
Random item first

questions.prompt: Which rule does a queue normally follow?
options: Last in, first out
First in, first out
Largest value first
Newest item only

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a software module?
options: Force all code into a single function
Remove the need for interfaces
Group related code behind a coherent responsibility or interface
Make every variable accessible from everywhere

questions.prompt: What does the DRY principle encourage?
options: Repeating the same rule in every file
Removing all documentation
Writing only one test per application
Avoiding unnecessary duplication of knowledge or logic

questions.prompt: In Python, what is total after: total = 0; then for i in range(1, 4): total += i?
An array has length n and uses zero-based indexing. Which loop condition avoids reading past its last element when i starts at 0?
options: i <= n
i < n
i == n

questions.prompt: In Python, def add(x, items=[]): items.append(x); return items is called twice without items. Why can the second call contain the first call's item?
options: Python deletes the argument after each call
Lists cannot hold more than one item
The default list is created once and shared between calls
Every function call resets all lists

questions.prompt: In Python: x = [1, 2]; y = x; y.append(3). What is x afterward?
A loop adds each value in [2, 4, 6] to a total initially equal to 0. What is the final total?
In Python: x = 5; y = x; y += 2. What is the value of x afterward?
What must be true of an array before ordinary binary search can correctly search it?
options: Every value must be different
Its length must be even
It must be sorted according to the comparison being used
It must contain only positive numbers

questions.prompt: A function divides a total by a user-supplied count. Which check directly prevents division by zero?
options: Check that the total is positive
Check that the count is even
Convert the total to a string
Check that the count is not zero before dividing

questions.prompt: Valid ages are from 18 through 60 inclusive. Which set best checks both boundaries and their immediately invalid neighbors?
A function should return abs(x), but a defect makes it return x unchanged. Which added test is most likely to expose the defect?
options: x = 7, expected 7
x = -7, expected 7
x = 0, expected 0
x = 12, expected 12

questions.prompt: A unit test must verify retry behavior without calling a real network service. What is the best approach?
options: Disable every assertion
Require a production outage before testing
Inject a fake or mock network client with controlled responses
Wait until the network fails randomly

questions.prompt: You want a Git commit to include changes in a tracked source file. Which normal sequence records those changes?
options: git status, then delete the repository
git log, then close the editor
git branch, then ignore the file
Stage the file with git add, then run git commit

questions.prompt: A function opens a file and may raise an exception while processing it. Which approach best ensures the file is closed?
options: Use a context manager or cleanup in a finally block
Close the file only after a successful calculation
Let the caller guess whether it is still open
Remove exception handling and hope processing succeeds

questions.prompt: A database query contains a user-supplied name. Which construction best prevents that input from being interpreted as SQL code?
options: Concatenate the name directly into the SQL string
Use a parameterized query with bound values
Remove spaces from the name and concatenate it
Trust the input whenever it comes from a web form

questions.prompt: What is a useful role of continuous integration for a shared repository?
options: Prevent developers from creating branches
Replace source control with a chat message
Automatically build and test changes when they are submitted
Guarantee that no production defect can ever occur

questions.prompt: The values A, B, and C are pushed onto an empty stack in that order. Which value is returned by the first pop?
options: A
B
All three values simultaneously
C

questions.prompt: In Python, which range visits every integer from 1 through n inclusive when n is positive?
options: range(1, n + 1)
range(1, n)
range(0, n)
range(n + 1, 1)

questions.prompt: A catch block silently ignores every exception and returns a success message. What is the most appropriate improvement?
options: Keep the success message for every failure
Handle expected errors explicitly and preserve or report unexpected failures
Remove every test of the function
Change every exception into an empty comment

questions.prompt: One class validates user input, writes database records, and sends emails. Which change best supports the single-responsibility principle?
options: Put all three tasks into one longer method
Make every field global
Separate validation, persistence, and email responsibilities behind clear interfaces
Duplicate the class for every screen

questions.prompt: A test sends an HTTP request to the real application and checks a record written to a temporary database. What kind of test is this primarily?
options: A style-formatting check
A test of only a mathematical function
A manual code review
An integration test

questions.prompt: Why might a team deploy a new feature behind a feature flag?
options: To control exposure and enable a gradual rollout
To make automated tests unnecessary
To permanently remove all error logs
To guarantee the database will never fail

questions.prompt: In Python, what does set([1, 1, 2]) contain?
options: Three copies of 1
The two distinct values 1 and 2
Only the value 2
The list [1, 1, 2] as a single element

questions.prompt: Two threads read a shared counter before either writes its incremented value. The counter increases only once instead of twice. What happened?
options: A guaranteed compiler optimization
A successful atomic update
A race condition causing a lost update
An array boundary error

questions.prompt: A test for expiry depends directly on the current system time and fails intermittently. What change makes the test more deterministic?
options: Increase the number of random delays
Remove all expiry checks
Run the test only at midnight
Inject a controllable clock and set the test time explicitly

questions.prompt: A loop runs i from 1 through n. For each i, an inner loop performs i constant-time operations. What is the overall time complexity?
options: O(n squared)
O(log n)
O(n)

questions.prompt: A naive recursive Fibonacci function calls fib(n - 1) and fib(n - 2), with constant-time base cases and no memoization. How does its running time grow?
options: Constantly with n
Exponentially with n
Only logarithmically with n
Exactly linearly with n

questions.prompt: A transfer subtracts money from account A and adds it to account B. If the second write fails, what best prevents a partial transfer from being committed?
options: Log the failure but commit the first write
Retry only the subtraction
Execute both writes in one database transaction and roll back on failure
Update the screen before either write completes

questions.prompt: A client times out after submitting a payment and retries the same request. Which design best prevents charging the customer twice?
options: Assign a different payment identifier on every retry
Assume timeouts always mean the payment failed
Remove transaction boundaries to speed up retries
Use a stable idempotency key and atomically store the payment result for that key

questions.prompt: Thread A acquires lock X then waits for Y; thread B acquires Y then waits for X. Which general design change best prevents this deadlock pattern?
options: Require all threads to acquire these locks in the same global order
Add more unrelated locks
Remove all transaction error messages
Make both threads wait longer before acquiring their second lock

questions.prompt: Two users load record version 16. The first saves and creates version 17. With optimistic concurrency control, what should happen to the second user's save carrying version 16?
options: It should silently overwrite version 17
It should be rejected as a conflict and require review against the latest version
It should delete both users' changes
It should reset the server's version back to 16

questions.prompt: A cached formatter's output depends on both an amount and a locale. Results for different locales are being mixed. What is the most appropriate fix?
options: Cache only the first result forever
Remove the locale from the formatting function without changing its requirements
Include both the amount and locale in the cache key
Use only the current minute as the cache key

questions.prompt: Which combination of properties best checks a sorting function for arbitrary lists?
options: Its output always has at least one element
Its output removes all repeated values
Its output always starts with zero
The output is ordered, preserves the input multiset, and sorting it again gives the same result

questions.prompt: A subtype refuses some inputs that the base type's documented contract accepts. Which object-oriented principle is most directly violated?
options: The Liskov substitution principle
The rule that source files need an extension
The requirement that every method be static
The rule that arrays start at zero

questions.prompt: In Java, two objects are equal according to equals(), but their hashCode() values differ. Why can this break their use in a HashSet?
options: HashSet requires every object to use a unique class name
Equal objects must have equal hash codes so hash-based lookup can find them consistently
HashSet compares only the lengths of object names
Overriding equals() automatically deletes the set's contents

questions.prompt: An API checks that a seat is available, then inserts a booking. Two concurrent requests can both pass the check and book the same seat. What best enforces a single booking?
options: Repeat the availability check only in the user interface
Wait one second between the check and insert
Use a database uniqueness constraint with transactional booking and handle conflicts
Remove the seat identifier from the booking record

questions.prompt: A message consumer can receive the same event more than once. It updates a balance and records the processed event ID. What best prevents duplicate balance updates, including after crashes?
options: Update the balance first and record the event ID in a separate later transaction
Ignore event IDs and rely on network delivery order
Generate a fresh event ID whenever a duplicate arrives
Check or insert a unique event ID and update the balance atomically in the same transaction
